podcast.title: Donna's Domain Review
podcast.body: The guitarist from Orgy was rated "average" in terms of sexual ability and penis size on Donna's Domain. The review also noted he had "some specific kinks," was "a good kisser," but possessed "the personality of a corpse." "The guitarist is average. Although he has some specific kinks that I really can't get into here. He's also a good kisser, but he has the personality of a corpse."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Escaped New Metal Classification
podcast.body: Orgy was initially categorized under the heading of new metal but eventually escaped that classification, a goal many bands fought hard to achieve. "Orgy... Most eventually escaped that classification, something that many fought very hard to do."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Jay Gordon's Contribution to Linkin Park Remix
podcast.body: Jay Gordon, the singer for the San Francisco band Orgy, provided a new vocal track for the reinterpreted mix of Linkin Park's song "Points of Authority," featured on Linkin Park's 2002 remix album, Reanimation. "The new voice in the track is from Jay Gordon, the singer for San Francisco band called Orgy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Members in Dead by Sunrise
podcast.body: Friends from the band Orgy were featured as members in Chester Bennington's side project, Dead by Sunrise, helping to form the group's lineup. "created this new group featuring some friends from bands called Julian K and Orgy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: New Metal Follower
podcast.body: Orgy was listed as one of the groups that emerged in the wake of successful new metal bands, indicating their association with the genre's sound and popularity. "Others followed. Stained. Orgy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
